documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M here to set up primary care. Transferring from a prior PCP office.

HIV since birth (mother HIV+). Followed by an outside ID clinic every ~6 mo, on Biktarvy 1 tab daily, which ID prescribes. Per pt last viral load was undetectable and CD4 'in the 600s'. No OIs that he knows of. Also genital HSV-2, on valacyclovir 500 daily for suppression for years; rare breakthrough, none recently.

PSH: circumcised as a newborn, nothing else.
Meds: Biktarvy daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Allergies: none to meds.
FH: mother HIV+. Father - doesn't know his history. Maternal grandmother with type 2 DM.
SH: works as a logistics coordinator for a distribution company. Never smoked. A drink or two on weekends. No IV or other drug use. Single, sexually active, more than one partner; says he uses condoms.
COVID: two Pfizer doses this spring at a pharmacy.

ROS: negative except as above.
Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, no thrush. No cervical/axillary nodes. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Skin without rash. GU deferred.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. HIV, perinatal, stable per report - continue care with ID. Records requested. Will keep copies of their labs here.
2. Genital HSV-2 - continue valacyclovir; I can handle refills.
3. Health maintenance - PCV20 and first MenACWY today (both recommended with HIV). Second MenACWY in 8 wk, nurse visit. Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids, UA.
Follow up yearly for physical, sooner prn.

conditions.label: Thrombocytopenia
conditions.note: Isolated; in the setting of non-suppressed HIV

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ~2 wk of bruises he can't account for, then a speckled red rash on both lower legs. No nosebleeds, gum bleeding, blood in urine or stool. No fever, no recent illness. No new meds, no OTC NSAIDs or supplements. Asked about the Biktarvy - honest that he is still missing doses, maybe 2-3 a week.

O: Afebrile. Pinpoint non-blanching petechiae over both shins, a few 2-3 cm bruises on thighs and forearms. Mouth: no blood blisters. No cervical, axillary or inguinal nodes. Spleen not palpable. Heart/lungs normal.

CBC sent stat: platelets 31. Hgb and WBC normal.

A/P: isolated thrombocytopenia with petechiae. With his viral load up in March, HIV-related platelet destruction is the leading thought, but needs hematology.
- Called outside hematology, they will see him Wed 8/23.
- No NSAIDs/aspirin, no contact sports, ER precautions reviewed.
- Adherence: again, every day. He agreed to set up a weekly pill box.
- Will update ID.

documents.title: Call to Hematology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with hematology on call re plt 31, petechiae, HIV not suppressed. Urgent slot Wed. Pt informed by phone, he can make it.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY CONSULTATION - outside hematology/oncology group
Date seen: 08/23/2023
Referred by: primary care, for low platelets

HPI: 33-year-old man with HIV acquired at birth and genital HSV-2, on Biktarvy and valacyclovir, last at his ID clinic about six months ago. Two weeks of bruising with little provocation and pinpoint spots on the lower legs. No infections in recent weeks and no new medications or supplements. Admits inconsistent ART use since early this year.

Allergies: NKDA
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily
FH: mother with HIV. Father unknown. Maternal grandmother type 2 diabetes.
SH: logistics coordinator. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks/week.

Exam: petechiae both lower legs. Liver and spleen not enlarged. No lymph node enlargement anywhere.

Data:
- Platelets 25 x10^9/L, Hgb 14 g/dL, WBC 6.5 x10^9/L
- Smear reviewed personally: red and white cells look normal; platelets few but normal in appearance. Isolated thrombocytopenia.
- PT/INR, aPTT normal
- As part of our standard workup for isolated thrombocytopenia: HCV antibody negative; HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab reactive and HIV-1 RNA detected, in keeping with his known, currently unsuppressed infection.

Assessment: isolated thrombocytopenia, most likely HIV-associated, driven by uncontrolled viremia.

Recommendations:
1. The main treatment here is getting his virus back under control - daily ART without missed doses. Discussed with him at length.
2. Bleeding precautions; no NSAIDs or aspirin.
3. CBC weekly to start (can be drawn at his PCP office), then spacing out.
4. Seek care for any bleeding.
Will see him back in about 3 months, sooner if counts drop.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Visit - Genital Ulcer
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Date of visit: 9/3/2025

CC: sore on the penis x3 weeks.

He noticed a sore on the shaft about three weeks ago. It doesn't hurt, hasn't grown or shrunk, and nothing drains from it. He has felt some swelling in both groins. Different from his usual herpes - no tingling, no blisters. Multiple partners, condoms not every time.

Allergies: NKDA.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily; valacyclovir 500 mg daily.

Exam: single firm, indurated ulcer on the penile shaft, clean base, not tender. Both inguinal regions with enlarged, non-tender nodes.

Labs: RPR non-reactive. TP-PA reactive. HIV RNA not detected on today's draw.

Assessment: primary syphilis. A non-reactive RPR this early is not unusual; the treponemal test and the classic painless indurated chancre make the diagnosis.

Plan:
- Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM, one dose, given today. Observed 30 min, no reaction.
- Partner notification through the state health department; he was given the DIS contact.
- Abstain until the ulcer heals and partners are treated.
- Return in about 3 months with repeat RPR.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - outside hospital
Arrival 02/23/2026 19:40

Chief complaint: L testicle pain and swelling x 2 days, burning with urination, penile discharge.

HPI: 35M with perinatally acquired HIV (on ART), HSV-2, and syphilis treated last fall. Two days of worsening left testicular pain and swelling. Lying down with the scrotum propped up helps some. Over the same stretch, burning when he urinates and a whitish, milky drip from the penis. Several partners, condoms not consistently.

Allergies: NKDA
Home meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, valacyclovir 500 mg daily

Vitals: T 38.3 C (100.9 F), BP 130/80, HR 88.

Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. Left testis swollen and tender, sitting higher than the right. Lifting the scrotum eases the pain (Prehn sign positive). Cremasteric reflex present. Right side normal.

Results: UA with pyuria and positive leukocyte esterase. Urine NAAT: Chlamydia trachomatis positive, N. gonorrhoeae negative.

ED course / MDM: presentation fits epididymitis, most likely sexually transmitted given urethritis symptoms; preserved cremasteric reflex and relief with elevation favor this over torsion. Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in the ED; tolerated. Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 days prescribed.

Disposition: discharged home 00:15. Scrotal support, ice, rest. Abstain from sex until treatment finished and partners treated. Follow up with PCP within a week. Return for worsening pain, high fever or vomiting.

Diagnosis: acute left epididymitis, chlamydial.

documents.title: Post-ED Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received. Called pt: on day 2 of doxycycline, taking it with food, fever gone, pain a little better. Booked PCP f/u 3/3.

Pain and swelling way down, burning with urination gone, no more discharge. No fever since the first day. Some stomach upset with the doxy, manageable with meals.
Hasn't had sex since; he notified his partners and says they're getting treated.

Exam: afebrile. Testes symmetric, no swelling, non-tender, no masses. No urethral discharge. No inguinal nodes.

A/P: chlamydial epididymitis, responding.
- Finish doxycycline.
- Retest chlamydia ~3 months out - will do at his physical, booked 5/1.
- Condoms; discussed that he's had two bacterial STIs in 6 months.
RTC 5/1.

NKDA. Never smoker. 1-2 drinks most weeks. Still at the logistics job.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. GU: testes normal size, non-tender, no masses. Skin without lesions.

A/P
1. HIV, perinatal - suppressed, ID following q6 months.
2. Genital HSV-2 - quiet on valacyclovir; refilled.
3. Chlamydial epididymitis - clinically resolved; urine GC/CT retest sent today.
4. Primary syphilis 2025 - treated per ID.
5. HM - Tdap 2025, hep A series done, PCV20 2021;  Flu/COVID in the fall. CMP, CBC, lipids.
Follow-up in September.
